Middle East.headline: Israeli airstrikes , operations in Gaza, a woman killed in the West Bank
Middle East.body: Gaza – In recent hours, various areas of the Gaza Strip witnessed an escalation of violence, resulting in injuries and material damage. In the northern Gaza Strip, Israeli military vehicles entered the Al-Amoudi area, coinciding with artillery shelling and gunfire targeting homes and tents of displaced people west of Beit Lahia, resulting in injuries. Middle East.body: WEST BANK / PNN / A 60-year-old Palestinian woman, Fadda Mohammed Fheidat, was killed and 10 others wounded by settler gunfire in the Deir Qult al-Tahta area of Jericho, in the eastern occupied West Bank, on Monday evening, according to Jericho Governmental Hospital. Americas.headline: How to help victims of deadly Venezuela earthquakes - ABC News
Americas.body: How to help victims of deadly Venezuela earthquakes Scores of people were killed and hundreds have been injured. Relief efforts are underway after a pair of powerful earthquakes struck north-central Venezuela on Wednesday evening, killing more than 160 people and injuring almost 1,000 as of Thursday morning. Emergency responders were undertaking "intensive rescue operations" early Thursday, searching for people thought to be under the rubble, Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodriguez said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he spoke with Rodriguez and that the U.S. is sending search and rescue teams to the country. Americas.headline: Canada Signs Ebola Pact With Africa CDC but Lists No Funding, Vaccine Doses or Duration
Americas.body: Africa CDC announced a memorandum of understanding with the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) on Nov. 16, covering surveillance, laboratories and medical countermeasures, but the announcement states no funding, vaccine doses or duration. It arrives as the Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 11,042 confirmed cases and at least 5,387 deaths across eight of the country's 26 provinces, according to government figures released Nov. 10. Africa.headline: 6 months of the Ebola outbreak in the Congo: War, hunger, disease and profit
Africa.body: “The virus is the spark. The structural conditions are the accelerant.” These words from Dr. Tyler Evans, an infectious disease specialist who worked in West Africa and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), summarize the unfolding catastrophe. Six months ago, on May 17, the World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) over eight laboratory-confirmed cases across three health zones in Ituri Province. Today, official bulletins record 11,254 confirmed cases and 5,505 confirmed deaths across 68 health zones in eight provinces, establishing this outbreak as the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record. Africa.headline: Chinese National Abducted, Two Killed in DR Congo During Deadly Ambush at Kalemie
Africa.body: A Chinese national has been abducted in the Democratic Republic of Congo and is still missing. The Chinese man was kidnapped after armed men ambushed a convoy on the Kalemie-Bendera road in the Tanganyika Province of DR Congo. Two people were killed during the incident, including a soldier belonging to the National Military of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and a mining company employee, while the driver of the vehicle they were traveling in was seriously wounded. Authorities in DRC say security forces are pursuing the kidnappers and searching for their Chinese hostage. Africa.headline: UNICEF: Children make up 35% of Ebola deaths in DR Congo outbreak
Africa.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to hit children hardest, with children representing 28% of total cases but 35% of deaths, according to a new report from UNICEF. Few children are being seen at Ebola treatment centers, UNICEF said, and if they do arrive at a facility, one in three children ages 5 years and under die within 24 hours. The outbreak has also resulted in 2,280 children orphaned or separated from their families since the epidemic began in May. Asia-Pacific.headline: Dozens of Civilians Killed in Myanmar Regime Strikes as ASEAN Leaders Meet
Asia-Pacific.body: The Myanmar regime has continued bombing civilian targets nationwide after its leaders were barred from attending the ongoing 49th ASEAN Summit for rejecting the bloc’s peace plan. Rakhine State has borne the brunt of attacks, which have killed over a dozen civilians in the past week as the ethnic Arkan Army (AA) pushes to seize the state capital, Sittwe, and Kyaukphyu, home to China-backed mega projects. Junta warplanes pounded residential areas in the AA-held town of Kyauktaw on Monday night, but casualty figures were unclear as of press time. Asia-Pacific.headline: A strong earthquake struck Indonesia
Asia-Pacific.body: A strong earthquake struck Indonesia A magnitude 6.6 earthquake was recorded in Indonesia. This was reported by the United States Geological Survey (USGS). According to seismologists, the tremors were recorded on Monday at 21:11 Coordinated Universal Time. The epicenter of the earthquake was located 151 kilometers from the Indonesian city of Tual, which is home to approximately 89,000 people. The focus of the seismic activity was at a depth of 35 kilometers. There is no information about injuries, deaths, or destruction.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Ebola outbreak defies control as war and hunger fuel crisis six months in
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Six months into the biggest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s history, containing the virus increasingly depends on solving problems far beyond Ebola — hunger, armed conflict, mistrust and a health system already buckling under the strain. More than 11,000 people have been infected and 5,500 have died since the outbreak was declared May 15. Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Bhubaneswar: With another cyclonic storm threatening the east coast, Odisha has stepped up its disaster preparedness, deploying 74 rescue teams and initiating precautionary evacuations in vulnerable districts. Cyclone Akvan, the third cyclonic storm to develop over the Bay of Bengal in three weeks, is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast on November 20. The Odisha government has directed district administrations to evacuate people living in landslide-prone and low-lying areas, particularly in the southern parts of the state. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Magnitude 5.7 earthquake strikes near Arthur’s Pass
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: A magnitude 5.7 earthquake near Arthur’s Pass was felt in Christchurch and Greymouth and woke some people in Rangiora. GeoNet said the quake struck at 11.30pm on Tuesday, 15 kilometres east of Arthur’s Pass, at a depth of 5 kilometres. It classified the shaking as strong. Its initial automatic reading put the quake at magnitude 5.4 and a depth of 14 kilometres. A second quake struck 14 minutes later, at 11.44pm. GeoNet recorded the magnitude 3.2 quake 15 kilometres southeast of Arthur’s Pass, also at a depth of 5 kilometres, and classified the shaking as weak.
